WHAT THIS FILE IS. The observed ENVELOPE of every entry the speed gate measures — the range it was actually seen over, with a tolerance, and never a single number pretending to be one. Recorded on the cell that reads it: ubuntu-latest, image ubuntu24/20260927.320, runner 2.337.0.

FOUR WINDOWS, TWO OF THEM QUIET AND ONE OBVIOUSLY NOT. The renderer workloads ship IDENTICAL CODE at every commit these windows cover; the rounds between them touched the workflow, the tests, the comparator and this document, never a renderer:

    window 1  07:46-07:56Z  at 3c30eca  runs 36832215161 36832519319 36832824918 36833056763
    window 2  10:15-10:24Z  at 4c003c6  runs 36847969226 36848207890 36848474648 36848721383
    window 3  10:35-10:47Z  at 94e8a78  runs 36850024437 36850406095 36850650070 36850880222 36851111411
    window 4  2026-10-01    at 0f767ce  runs 36855858404 36856381088 36856708238

    entry                         window 1        window 2        window 3        window 4
    counter::unit-suite            16.593-23.203   22.852-24.544   21.657-24.360   16.333-23.603
    e2e::bench.render               0.056- 0.084     0.080- 0.087     0.079- 0.084     0.057- 0.082
    e2e::bench.render-impact        1.019- 1.351     1.332- 1.404     1.045- 1.355     0.956- 1.346
    e2e::bench.render-responsiveness 0.060- 0.080     0.078- 0.086     0.078- 0.082     0.059- 0.080

THE SPREAD IS NOT A PROPERTY OF THE WORKLOAD. It is the workload AND the state of the pool during the window. Windows 2 and 3 were quiet and windows 1 and 4 were not, on the same cell, the same image and the same programs — window 4's suite spans 16.332520 against a body around 22-23.6, the same shape as window 1. A tolerance derived from the quiet windows alone would have been far too tight, and a quiet window is not a measurement of the cell; it is a measurement of a quiet afternoon. THAT IS WHY NOTHING HERE IS DERIVED FROM THE MOST RECENT RUNS.

WHY THE RENDERER ENVELOPES SPAN FOUR WINDOWS AND THE SUITE'S DOES NOT. The renderers and WORKLOADS are unchanged since 3c30eca, so all sixteen dispatches measure one program and their union is that program's observed range. The unit suite is different: each window measured a tree with a different number of collected tests — 770, 777, 780, 784 — because the controls governing this document were being added between them. Those are different programs, and the renderer's justification for unioning does not transfer to them. The suite's envelope is therefore window 4 ALONE, which is the first window that measured THIS tree, and its spread of 44.5% is this suite's own observed figure rather than one inherited from a neighbour. Its tolerance is the rule's own answer to that figure: 0.45.

AN EARLIER REVISION OF THIS FILE RECORDED MAXIMA OF 0.090278, 1.414891 AND 0.087334 for the three workloads — figures carried from a summary table rather than derived from the runs, two of which exceeded every observation in the artifacts they cited, and the third attributed to the wrong window. Those maxima were replaced with the ones the artifacts contain and have not moved since. The error was in the safe direction — every recorded maximum clears every per-run minimum, so no run the cell has shown can false-red — but "the union of the runs" is a claim about the runs and it has to be one.

WHY THE TOLERANCES ARE WHAT THEY ARE — A STRUCTURAL ARGUMENT, NOT AN EMPIRICAL ONE. This gate compares a per-run MINIMUM against a recorded MAXIMUM. Its false-red risk comes from the head landing HIGH, above the recorded maximum. Folding the observed spread in as a single fraction covers the LOW tail too, which this gate cannot be hurt by. The rule is therefore conservative by construction: it measures in one direction and protects in the other. That is the correct side to err on for a gate whose failure mode is a red on main that teaches people to ignore it, and it is why the tolerances are the observed spreads rather than something tighter.

What the data does NOT support is a claim this file previously made, that the suite's tolerance was held at 0.40 to stop it false-reding on a busy run. Window 1's 39.8% for the suite was a LOW-tail artefact — one run at 16.6 against a body of 22.2-23.2 — so it was evidence of one fast machine, not of a busy pool. That claim is withdrawn. The suite's tolerance MOVED, from 0.40 to 0.45, and the reason is not slack: it is the rule applied to this tree's own measurement instead of to one inherited from a neighbouring tree, whose 13.3% quiet-window spread understated what the cell actually does. A number that moves because the evidence moved is the discipline working; a number that moves because someone wanted it to is the thing this file exists to prevent.

WHAT THIS GATE THEREFORE CATCHES, AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. The honest summary is uncomfortable. At these tolerances a DOUBLED workload is caught on NO ENTRY AT ALL: every entry's ceiling — observed maximum x (1 + tolerance) — is cleared by doubling its observed minimum, the suite's own 44.5% spread being most of the reason. Tightening any of them to catch its doubling means going below its own observed spread — a ceiling the fastest machine already clears, which would fire on ordinary pool variation. A gate that cries wolf is deader than one with a documented blind spot, so bench.render is NOT tuned and neither are its siblings. The gate catches a gross step change and the gross wall smoke bound; it will not catch a 20% regression anywhere. Read "load-invariant counter" as "a quantity the machine's load does not reach", not as "a sharp budget".

THE GROSS WALL SMOKE BOUND. `wall` is an envelope for the same reason, spanning the same windows; at SMOKE_FACTOR 3.0 the ceilings are 164.6 seconds, 0.261, 4.69 and 0.261. `test_baseline.py` recomputes all four from this document, because a transcribed ceiling was wrong twice in this file's history. That bound is deliberately not a budget: it is a cliff detector for the class CPU cannot see at all, a workload getting slower in wall while its CPU cost holds flat, which is what blocking on I/O, a network call or a lock wait looks like. The report prints no elapsed time at all: a verdict and no number.

PROVENANCE. measured_commit is 0f767ce, the remote head the window-4 dispatches resolved --ref issue-81-82 against, and the suite's envelopes are from those runs. `population` is the digest of the node ids THIS tree collects, computed by running collect_node_ids over it rather than copied from anywhere, which is what the guard compares. The renderer envelopes describe this tree exactly — no renderer and no WORKLOADS entry has changed since 3c30eca.

Window 3's five dispatches exited non-zero: the suite's own population-digest control was red at that commit, because the baseline still described an older tree. The counters were recorded regardless, and the control was asserting about the document rather than about the work, so the measurements stand — but a dispatch whose suite is green is the cleaner source, and window 4 is one.

HOW TO RE-DERIVE. Run the job four or five times on the cell that will read it, and take each entry's min and max ACROSS dispatches AND across windows rather than within one. If the program is unchanged between trees, union the windows — that is what caught the fast machine no single window contained. If the program IS changed between them, do not: measure the one you ship, because a spread measured on a different program is not a spread you can budget against. Keep every window's figures either way. Re-derive, never carry, and never shrink because the latest runs were kind.

AND `population` MOVED AGAIN, FOR THE SAME REASON IT MOVES: the cross-platform round added five tests that check this instrument's behaviour where `resource` and `/proc` do not exist. The digest is recomputed from this tree rather than left to describe a neighbour, because a digest that no longer matches is the guard working and a digest edited forward by hand is the thing the guard exists to catch. The renderer envelopes are untouched by this round: no renderer, no WORKLOADS entry and no shipped module changed.

AND `population` MOVED AGAIN, for the same reason as every time: this round restored five controls and guarded twenty-four more, so the collected population is larger. Recomputed from this tree rather than left describing a neighbour. The renderer envelopes are untouched — no renderer, no WORKLOADS entry and no shipped module changed.

AND `population` MOVED ONCE MORE, because this round added the platform predicate and its controls. Recomputed from this tree, as always. The renderer envelopes are untouched — no renderer, no WORKLOADS entry and no shipped module changed.

AND `population` MOVED, because this round added two controls and a second platform predicate. Recomputed from this tree, as always. The renderer envelopes are untouched.

AFTER THE REBASE ONTO ada43c5. The renderer envelopes ARE UNCHANGED, and deliberately so: that rebase moved the coverage ratchet, its workflow and two test modules, and touched no renderer, no WORKLOADS entry, no bench harness and no fixture builder. Those envelopes describe the same program they described when the dispatches measured it, and re-measuring would replace a record of this tree with a record of the same tree.

The unit suite DID move, and only in identity rather than in cost: it now collects test_coverage_ratchet_ci.py and test_release_workflow.py, which the rebase changed. `population` is recomputed from this tree accordingly — the digest is what says which population the numbers were observed over, and a stale one is a document claiming something untrue about itself. Its CPU and wall envelopes are LEFT AS RECORDED, on the ground that two small test modules cannot move a 44.5% observed spread far enough to matter against a 0.45 tolerance: the recorded maximum is 23.60 CPU seconds and the ceiling is 34.1, and the ceiling has more headroom than the entire population change is wide. If the next dispatch shows the suite above the recorded maximum, that is the envelope working and it gets re-derived from those runs then; that is the correct time to spend a runner on it, not now.

AND `population` MOVED AGAIN, for the third time and for the same reason: this round added controls and guards, so the collected population is a different set of node ids. Recomputed from this tree. The renderer envelopes are untouched — no renderer, no WORKLOADS entry and no shipped module changed.

AND `population` MOVED, for the fourth time and the same reason: this round added a standing control over the guards themselves, so the collected population is a different set of node ids. Recomputed from this tree. The renderer envelopes are untouched.

AND `population` MOVED AGAIN, because this round added consolidated gate-selector tests for API failures, malformed paths and reporting, needs-verdict tests and workflow controls. Recomputed from this tree. The renderer envelopes are untouched.

AND population MOVED AGAIN, because the supersession tests now prove that an unknown current-run timestamp cannot excuse a cancellation. Recomputed from this tree with 808 collected tests. Renderer envelopes are untouched.

AND population MOVED in fix round 2: schedule ownership, tag-push classification, CodeQL path rules, and event-scoped supersession controls changed the collected test set. Recomputed from this tree with 815 collected tests. Renderer envelopes are untouched.

AND population MOVED in fix round 3: this round restores bare release-gate producers, scopes cancellation proof to the same PR, and adds regression controls for those rules. Recomputed from this tree with 827 collected tests. Renderer envelopes are untouched.

AND population MOVED in fix round 4: the concurrency control was renamed to pin its per-PR and per-run-id keys, changing one collected test node ID. Recomputed from this tree with 827 collected tests. Renderer envelopes are untouched.

AND population MOVED in fix round 2: this round adds fifteen unit controls. Recomputed from this tree with 880 collected tests.

AND population MOVED in fix round 3: this round adds the delayed-workload pipe regression control. Recomputed from this tree with 881 collected tests. Renderer envelopes are untouched.\n\nAND population MOVED again in round-3 review remediation: this round adds a control for quoted and sequence-item forms of the gitleaks error-swallowing key. Recomputed from this tree with 882 collected tests. Renderer envelopes are untouched.

RE-DERIVED AT 2901f4e (window 5, 2026-10-04) — THE FIRST ENVELOPE RE-DERIVATION, AND THE ONE ISSUE #133 EXISTS FOR. The committed envelope was measured at 0f767ce over a 784-test program; the tree it gates collects 988. A module-level CPU census on the box (35 modules, the repo's own counter.py instrument, 77.22 CPU s total) attributes the step: the PR-#131-family controls carry 26.6% of suite CPU, test_gate_base_freshness.py alone 11.94 s (15.5%) — the offline git-fixture controls spawn real git subprocesses per case, which is the cost of guarding the gates and is recorded here as a real cost step rather than absorbed as drift. Four workflow_dispatch runs of tests.yml at 2901f4e962e121d342b74ede43919ee1c6c4989b measured the new program: runs 37188224043, 37188228619, 37188232856, 37188236879. Folded per-run CPU (min across the two rounds of each run): 29.346049, 35.713517, 37.312567, 40.544835 — every observation above the old recorded maximum 23.602898, so the step is the population, not pool noise. Recorded envelope: min 29.346049, max 40.544835, n=4, span 38.2% from min. Tolerance stays 0.45: the control only demands tolerance >= the observed span, and 0.45 covers it; it is not tightened on four same-day dispatches because window 1 and window 4 both contained low tails no other window showed — a one-day window cannot bound this cell's spread. Wall 65.223-73.671 (n=4), same four runs. The renderer envelopes are untouched, but not because every observation fit. Runs 37188224043, 37188228619 and 37188232856 folded inside their recorded ranges; run 37188236879 folded ABOVE all six recorded renderer maxima (CPU 0.095879 / 1.518857 / 0.092003 against 0.089596 / 1.440689 / 0.087284; wall 0.096385 / 1.667559 / 0.092422 against 0.087 / 1.564 / 0.087), and run 37188232856's bench.render wall (0.088326) had already exceeded its recorded 0.087. Every excursion stays inside the gate's effective ceilings, CPU max x (1 + 0.6) and wall max x 3, which is why the gate passed throughout — and why the envelopes are RETAINED rather than raised: nothing derives renderer declarations, so a renderer ceiling cannot rise, and the honest record of that gap is this paragraph. The renderer envelope no longer contains the program's full observed range; the next lawful raise is the one where WORKLOADS changes. The doubling pin (test_baseline.py::test_a_doubled_workload_is_caught_wherever_the_gate_can) survives unchanged: 2 x 29.346049 = 58.692098 against ceiling 40.544835 x 1.45 = 58.79001075 — the doubled minimum misses the ceiling by 0.098 CPU s (0.17%), so 'a doubled workload is caught on NO entry' still holds, barely, and a flip on the next re-derivation is a deliberate act in that test. The down-only ratchet gained a declared-raise route in this same change (--ratchet-allow-raise, derived in the workflow for the unit-suite population only), because the rule as written had no green path for a documented re-derivation: every observation of the new program landed above the old recorded maximum.

AND THE `population` DIGEST MOVED WITH THE WORK IT DOCUMENTS: this change adds declaration and ratchet controls (unit cases in test_baseline.py, CLI cases in test_speed_workflow.py, and executed step-derivation controls in test_speed_ratchet.py), so the tree the envelope was re-derived over is not the tree it commits. Recomputed from the final tree with 1001 collected tests, per the digest rule the document has always followed; the value this change replaces described 988. The digest and the numbers in one commit is the point: a re-derivation that moves either half alone is the drift the guard exists to catch.
